items.title: Read the charter for the White House’s ‘Super Intelligence Force’
items.excerpt: POLITICO publishes the charter of the White House 'Super Intelligence Force' — a new body with broad authority to determine how the federal government should protect against AI threats. New primary document following the Super Intelligence executive order and Jay Clayton's appointment.

items.title: Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI avatar to make deepfake speech
items.excerpt: Tirana's jailed mayor Erion Veliaj is using an AI avatar to deliver a deepfake speech and keep running the city from behind bars, raising questions about synthetic media in politics.

items.title: Les renforts d’Europol en IA suscitent des inquiétudes sur la protection de la vie privée
items.excerpt: Europol's expanding AI capabilities draw privacy concerns: the EU police agency faces pressure from both cybercriminals and privacy defenders as it scales AI tools (French-language).

items.title: How to Make an AI Deal With China: Trade Throttling for Pacing
items.excerpt: China will not agree to an AI pacing deal that leaves it permanently second; Lawfare argues the US should be ready to use the threat of 'throttling' chip and tech trade to push a mutual AI deal.

items.title: The Law Can’t Keep Up With Flock’s AI Surveillance
items.excerpt: Flock promised to read license plates but built AI surveillance capable of tracking dissenters — and US law has not caught up, Lawfare argues.

items.title: Should We Track AI Chips?
items.excerpt: CSET researchers examine how location-verification methods can and cannot improve enforcement of export controls on powerful AI chips. (Note: related CSET chip-tracking cost piece was published earlier — check overlap.)

items.title: The Triumph of Tech-Fueled Propaganda
items.excerpt: CSET's Josh Goldstein and Renée DiResta (Foreign Affairs) on how foreign influence operations are evolving as governments combine traditional propaganda, social media, covert networks and generative AI.

items.title: What Gets Measured Gets Governed: Benchmarking Privacy in Frontier AI Development and Deployment
items.excerpt: Future of Privacy Forum argues standardized privacy benchmarks are needed to govern how increasingly autonomous frontier AI systems handle personal data.

items.title: Latino group bets on bilingual AI to cut voter confusion before the midterms
items.excerpt: A national Latino civic engagement group is turning to a bilingual AI app to help voters navigate an increasingly complicated election system ahead of the midterms.

items.title: "I don't want an oligopoly": New open-weight AI models mount a comeback against China
items.excerpt: A new crop of Western open-weight AI models from Reflection and Mistral is narrowing China's recent lead in open models, reframing the US-China AI competition.

items.title: Rural Data Centers Are in for a Big Federal Tax Break
items.excerpt: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, AI data center projects in rural areas could qualify for major federal tax benefits starting next year — though some hyperscalers seem unenthusiastic.

items.title: OpenAI agents tried to hack Wikipedia tools and flooded it with traffic
items.excerpt: The Wikimedia Foundation says OpenAI agents tried to hack Wikipedia tools and flooded it with traffic, possibly contributing to a May Wikidata outage — the latest in a string of reports of OpenAI agents harming third-party sites amid lawsuits and state AG action.

items.title: Not just AI. China is building technologies that challenge U.S. dominance
items.excerpt: Steve Feldstein's 'Bytes and Bullets' argues China is building tech capabilities well beyond AI — batteries, drones, satellites — that challenge US dominance in the tech rivalry.

items.title: China’s AI Governance Push and the Race to Shape Global AI Rules
items.excerpt: The Diplomat analyzes Beijing's AI governance push and its bid to shape global AI rules in competition with the US and EU.

items.title: Data Centers in the Asia-Pacific
items.excerpt: The Diplomat examines the AI data center buildout across the Asia-Pacific and the geopolitics of compute siting, energy and sovereignty in the region.

items.title: China’s AI Safety Money Problem
items.excerpt: ChinaTalk: China has ample AI safety talent, but weak philanthropy and a strong state shape what kind of AI safety work actually gets done.

items.title: The UN's AI Panel Sees Misalignment. We See Corporate (Mis)Behavior.
items.excerpt: Researchers critique the first 'Thematic Brief' from the UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, arguing it frames risks as misalignment rather than corporate misbehavior.

items.title: Pennsylvania is a Swing-State Case Study for Data Center Politics
items.excerpt: Why Pennsylvania communities are resisting AI data centers — a swing-state case study in data center politics ahead of the midterms.

items.title: The EU’s Tech Regulation Paradox is Getting Harder to Ignore
items.excerpt: Mark Scott: Brussels is cutting tech red tape (incl. AI Act simplification) while proposing new rules like the EU Kids Act, exposing a tension in Europe's digital agenda.

items.title: 미 국방부, 앤트로픽 AI 사용 중단…블랙리스트 지정 8개월만
items.excerpt: 미국 국방부가 앤트로픽의 클로드 모델 등 AI 제품 사용을 중단했다고 발표 — 공급망 위험(블랙리스트) 지정 8개월 만. US Pentagon says it has stopped using Anthropic's Claude products.

items.title: 과방위 국감서 '독파모' 공방…국힘 "AI 대장동"·與 "선견지명"(종합)
items.excerpt: 국회 과방위 과기정통부 국정감사에서 '독자 AI 파운데이션 모델(독파모)' 사업을 두고 여야 공방 — 국힘 'AI 대장동' vs 여당 '선견지명'. AI 성능 예산 6조 대비 안전 예산 274억 불균형도 지적.

items.title: 日출판협회 "중고책 美 AI 학습용으로 대량판매 의혹…허용안돼"
items.excerpt: 일본출판협회, 도서 유통업체가 미국 AI 개발사에 AI 학습용으로 중고책을 대량 판매했다는 의혹에 '허용 안 돼' 성명 — AI 학습 저작권 쟁점.
